f.title: Keep clinical trial records for 15 years
f.statement: Sponsors must keep clinical trial records for drugs and natural health products for 15 years (reduced from 25 years). The 15-year requirement applies to sponsors of clinical trials of all drugs and natural health products with ongoing record retention obligations before February 11, 2022, and of any new clinical trials authorized on or after February 11, 2022.
f.legal_basis: Food and Drug Regulations; Natural Health Products Regulations (amended by the Regulations Respecting Clinical Trials for Medical Devices and Drugs Relating to COVID-19)
f.applicability: Clinical trials of drugs and natural health products with ongoing retention obligations before 11 February 2022, and new clinical trials authorized on or after 11 February 2022
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.deadline: Retain records for 15 years from the date the record is created
rows.quote:
The requirement to keep records for 15 years would apply to sponsors of: 

 clinical trials of all drugs and natural health products with ongoing record retention obligations prior to February 11, 2022

 any new clinical trials authorized on or after February 11, 2022
rows.review_note: Review: 15 years expressed as 180 months in deadline_rule (the rule has no year unit). Double-check: the page's 'would apply' wording reports a binding regulatory amendment, so Mandatory; retention period, not a reporting clock.

deadline_rule.clock_start: the date the record is created
deadline_rule.applies_to: clinical trial records for drugs and natural health products

f.title: Start the record retention period on the date the record is created
f.statement: The 15-year period for keeping clinical trial records starts on the date the record is created.
f.legal_basis: Food and Drug Regulations; Natural Health Products Regulations
f.exceptions: Sponsors may instead start the clock for all study records when the trial is completed or terminated (see next row).

rows.quote: The period for keeping records starts on the date the record is created.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves the start point; Health Canada says it is consulting on the start date.

f.title: Sponsors may start the retention clock at trial completion or termination
f.statement: To simplify the process, sponsors may choose to start the retention clock for all study records when the trial is completed or terminated.

rows.quote: To simplify the process, sponsors may choose to "start the clock" for keeping all study records when the trial is completed or terminated.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: permission (may) proven by the quote.

dates.title: Health Canada notice: 15-year clinical trial record retention takes effect
dates.scope: Sponsors of clinical trials of drugs and natural health products (Food and Drug Regulations, Natural Health Products Regulations)
dates.quote: This change takes effect on February 11, 2022.
dates.timing_note: The Overview also states the amendments came into force on February 11, 2022. The page date 2022-03-28 is the page modification date, not a compliance date.
